title: Sign-ins survive resets
summary: A reset never rolls a sign-in back to the golden's older copy. Every test machine keeps two kinds of live login: harness logins and the identity profiles in ~/.yoke-browser-identities. The identity profiles are the machine's only browser login store; the installer, desktop missions and managed steps all open pages in them. Capture leaves these entries out of every golden, reset keeps them with their modes, and a copy an older golden sealed is never restored. Before clearing, Linux and WSL ask every Chromium to quit, and macOS closes each identity browser through its DevTools port, so the newest cookies are on disk. Linux and WSL keep the Claude, Codex and Cursor login files (.claude/.credentials.json, .codex/auth.json, .config/cursor/auth.json) live the same way, and no sign-in probe runs before clearing. Safari's cookie store and the snap Chromium store are no longer kept. A failed login is repaired by signing in again: harness logins on the host, identity logins with yoke browser authorize --test-machine. Live proof that logins survive a second reset is still owed.
